title: Cast Iron vs. PVC in Drainage Systems
description: Choosing between cast iron and PVC for drainage waste and vent (DWV) systems involves evaluating sound attenuation, fire resistance, and structural longevity. While PVC is lightweight, cost-effective, and corrosion-resistant, it easily transmits fluid flow noise through walls. Cast iron pipe, joined with heavy-duty shield couplings, significantly dampens acoustic vibration, making it the preferred choice for multi-family residential stacks and commercial buildings. Additionally, cast iron is non-combustible and won't contribute to smoke spread in fire-rated assemblies. Selecting the correct material depends on project noise requirements and local fire safety codes.
